rule: An acquired source candidate is not a produced runtime event. Human listening, edit/derivation provenance and later Unity/device QA remain separate gates.

events.candidateFit: Natural public-domain stereo recording made at Litchfield Beach with MiniDisc and an AudioTechnica stereo microphone. It proves a real coastal/beach source, not that wind dominates over surf/water.
events.next: Human listening must decide whether there is enough clean coastal air/wind character for CoastalWind without surf becoming the wrong semantic layer. Reject or repurpose if the recording reads primarily as beach/waves.
Acquire natural palm/frond canopy movement with clean long regions and no preview artifacts.
Acquire broadleaf/jungle canopy wind with enough clean material for distinct temporal edits.

events.candidateFit: Natural public-domain source recorded during a walk in the Guadeloupean rainforest. It is location/biome-relevant, but metadata explicitly tags birds/birdsong and the moving-recordist perspective may be too active for a stable deep bed.
events.next: Human listening for footsteps/handling, close-bird dominance, noise and stable low-detail regions. Do not reuse this source as Jungle_CanopyWind without separate evidence.

events.candidateFit: Existing CC0 open-field wind recording is a plausible exposed-ridge texture but was recorded in a public park, not on a literal ridge.
events.next: Human headset/source listening for exposed-hill character, contamination and speech space before any derived ridge bed.
Acquire natural rough sea plus strong wind; current short beach-wave source is not promoted to storm-ocean coverage.

events.candidateFit: Long natural public-domain stereo wind recording from Fisterra. It is a plausible source pool for storm gust attacks/bodies/tails, but source duration and location do not prove ten genuinely distinct usable gust events.
events.next: Human listening and segmentation audit for clean outdoor gusts, contamination, headroom and genuinely distinct event shapes before derivation.

events.candidateFit: Natural public-domain thunder recorded in Southern Finland on Minidisc by the uploader. Metadata proves thunder and provenance, but not perceived near-event distance; decoded Vorbis also shows an explicit headroom risk that must be handled in any derivative.
events.next: Human listening for perceived proximity, transient quality, contamination and natural tail. If selected, derive with explicit headroom and re-run listening QA.

events.candidateFit: Two independently recorded public-domain Herring Gull source files with Bird/Gull/Shore provenance. Both are historical 22.05 kHz mono PDSounds-derived Ogg files and therefore need codec/context listening rather than automatic promotion.
events.next: Human listening for call isolation, codec artifacts, background contamination and island-context fit. Preserve them as two natural source events; do not inflate variation count with pitch/gain-only copies.

events.candidateFit: Natural backyard cricket recording; technically intact but low-level and recorded with a laptop built-in microphone.
events.next: Human listening for noise floor, biome fit and genuinely distinct chirp clusters before derivation.

events.candidateFit: Existing CC0 wood-burning fireplace source is a plausible source for isolated dry pops/crackles; it has not been proven to yield fourteen genuinely distinct usable events.
events.next: Human transient/listening review and segmentation audit; no gain-only duplicates.
